email: Hi, I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Can you check my invoice?
expected_summary: The customer was charged twice for a subscription and wants the invoice checked.
notes: Tests clear duplicate-charge language and invoice terminology.

email: I cannot log in to my account and need help resetting my password.
expected_summary: The customer cannot log in and needs help resetting the account password.
notes: Tests a straightforward login and password-recovery support request.

email: Can someone send me pricing details for your enterprise plan?
expected_summary: The customer is requesting pricing information for the enterprise plan.
notes: Tests an explicit pre-purchase enterprise pricing enquiry.

email: Congratulations, you are a winner! Click here to claim free money now.
expected_summary: The message claims the recipient won free money and urges them to click a link.
notes: Tests obvious prize-scam language and a suspicious call to action.

email: Hello, I wanted to ask about your office opening hours.
expected_summary: The sender is asking about the office opening hours.
notes: Tests a general informational request outside product and account support.

email: The payment failed but my card was still charged.
expected_summary: The customer's payment failed even though the card was charged.
notes: Tests billing precedence when a failed transaction could resemble a technical problem.

email: The dashboard keeps showing an error when I upload a file.
expected_summary: The customer encounters a dashboard error while uploading a file.
notes: Tests a clear reproducible product malfunction.

email: We would like to book a product demo for our team.
expected_summary: The sender wants to schedule a product demonstration for a team.
notes: Tests a direct sales-intent request for a product demo.

email: You have been selected for a limited-time cash prize.
expected_summary: The message claims the recipient was selected for a limited-time cash prize.
notes: Tests prize language without an explicit malicious link or call to action.

email: Please update my mailing address in your records.
expected_summary: The customer wants the mailing address in the records updated.
notes: Tests an administrative account request that is not troubleshooting.

email: Can you help me understand the pricing for your enterprise package?
expected_summary: The customer wants clarification about enterprise package pricing.
notes: Tests sales intent phrased as a request for help.

email: The app crashed while I was paying and I think I was charged twice.
expected_summary: The app crashed during payment and the customer believes a duplicate charge occurred.
notes: Tests billing versus support when a technical failure also causes a financial issue.

email: Please change my account email address. Nothing is broken.
expected_summary: The customer wants the email address on the account changed.
notes: Tests an administrative account change explicitly distinguished from technical troubleshooting.

email: Your trial expires today. Reply with your password now to avoid losing access.
expected_summary: The message threatens loss of trial access and asks the recipient to reply with a password.
notes: Tests phishing disguised as a legitimate trial-expiry notice by requesting a password.

email: My payment page keeps displaying an error before I can submit my card.
expected_summary: The payment page shows an error before the customer can submit card details.
notes: Tests support versus billing when no charge or completed transaction occurred.

email: Refund?
expected_summary: The sender is asking about a refund.
notes: Tests an extremely short billing message with almost no context.

email: i got chrgd 29.99 agin pls fix
expected_summary: The customer reports being charged 29.99 again and wants the charge corrected.
notes: Tests billing classification when the message contains several typos.

email: Me cobraron dos veces por la suscripción, can you refund one charge?
expected_summary: The customer says the subscription was charged twice and requests one charge be refunded.
notes: Tests a mixed Spanish-English duplicate-charge and refund request.

email: Love paying for the same month twice. Please reverse the second charge.
expected_summary: The customer sarcastically reports a duplicate monthly charge and requests its reversal.
notes: Tests whether sarcasm obscures a clear duplicate-charge complaint.

email: My plan renewed yesterday, but I thought the quoted price included the discount.
expected_summary: The customer disputes the price charged when the plan renewed.
notes: Tests billing versus sales when a prior quote is mentioned after renewal.

email: The refund shows as completed in your email, but the money is not back in my account.
expected_summary: The customer has not received a refund that was reported as completed.
notes: Tests a post-transaction refund-status problem.

email: Could you reissue last month's invoice with our VAT number shown?
expected_summary: The customer wants last month's invoice reissued with a VAT number.
notes: Tests invoice administration that belongs to billing rather than general other.

email: Login broken.
expected_summary: The customer reports that login is not working.
notes: Tests an extremely short but technically specific support request.

email: uplod gets stck at 99% evry time
expected_summary: The customer's uploads repeatedly get stuck at 99 percent.
notes: Tests recognition of a reproducible technical issue despite typos.

email: L'application se bloque après connexion, and then the screen stays white.
expected_summary: The application freezes after login and displays a white screen.
notes: Tests a mixed French-English application failure.

email: Fantastic update—now the dashboard crashes whenever I open reports.
expected_summary: The customer sarcastically reports that opening reports crashes the dashboard.
notes: Tests a technical complaint expressed through sarcasm.

email: The checkout spinner never stops, but no payment has been submitted or charged.
expected_summary: The checkout page remains loading before any payment is submitted or charged.
notes: Tests support versus billing with an explicit absence of a transaction.

email: I replaced my phone and now the two-factor code never arrives.
expected_summary: The customer cannot receive a two-factor authentication code after replacing a phone.
notes: Tests an account-access problem requiring technical troubleshooting.

email: POST /v1/orders returns 500 only when the optional note field is present.
expected_summary: The orders API returns a server error when the optional note field is included.
notes: Tests a precise developer-facing API defect.

email: Price?
expected_summary: The sender is asking for pricing information.
notes: Tests an extremely short sales enquiry with minimal context.

email: cn we get a dmo for 20 ppl nxt wk?
expected_summary: The sender requests a demo for 20 people next week.
notes: Tests demo intent in a typo-heavy message.

email: ¿Cuánto cuesta el plan empresarial for a team of 80 users?
expected_summary: The sender asks for enterprise plan pricing for a team of 80 users.
notes: Tests a mixed Spanish-English enterprise pricing request.

email: I suppose asking for a volume discount before buying 200 seats is wildly unreasonable?
expected_summary: The sender sarcastically asks about a volume discount for 200 seats.
notes: Tests sales intent expressed as a sarcastic rhetorical question.

email: We already use the basic plan and may add 40 seats; what would the new annual price be?
expected_summary: An existing customer is considering 40 additional seats and asks for annual pricing.
notes: Tests sales expansion versus billing for an existing customer before purchase.

email: Procurement needs a formal quote and security documentation before we can purchase.
expected_summary: The sender needs a formal quote and security documents before purchasing.
notes: Tests enterprise procurement intent beyond a simple pricing question.

email: Does the trial include SSO, or would we need to buy the business tier to test it?
expected_summary: The sender asks whether SSO can be tested in the trial or requires a business-tier purchase.
notes: Tests sales versus support when asking about features and trial eligibility.

email: WINNER!!!
expected_summary: The message emphatically claims that the recipient is a winner.
notes: Tests an extremely short message containing a classic spam signal.

email: Clik hear 2 recive ur FREE gift card, offer ends tonite!!!
expected_summary: The message urges the recipient to click to receive a free gift card before an urgent deadline.
notes: Tests scam recognition despite deliberate misspellings.

email: Has ganado €5,000! Reply with your bank details para recibir el premio.
expected_summary: The message claims a 5,000 euro prize and requests bank details to receive it.
notes: Tests a mixed Spanish-English prize scam requesting sensitive information.

email: This is definitely a totally legitimate investment—send crypto today and double it tomorrow.
expected_summary: The message promises to double a cryptocurrency payment within one day.
notes: Tests a sarcastically framed investment scam with unrealistic returns.

email: OVERDUE INVOICE: Open the attached ZIP and enable macros to avoid legal action.
expected_summary: The message uses an overdue-invoice claim and legal threat to induce opening a ZIP file and enabling macros.
notes: Tests spam versus billing when invoice language accompanies strong malware-delivery indicators.

email: Your mailbox will be deleted in 30 minutes. Verify your password at this link.
expected_summary: The message threatens immediate mailbox deletion and asks the recipient to verify a password through a link.
notes: Tests phishing indicators involving urgency and a password-verification link versus legitimate account support.

email: Dear website owner, we guarantee page-one rankings. Buy 10,000 backlinks today.
expected_summary: The sender guarantees page-one rankings and offers 10,000 backlinks.
notes: Tests a generic bulk SEO promotion with an implausible guarantee.

email: Hours?
expected_summary: The sender asks about unspecified hours.
notes: Tests a context-free, ambiguous query for which other is the safest fallback.

email: pls chnge my postl adress to 14 Lake Rd
expected_summary: The customer wants the postal address changed to 14 Lake Road.
notes: Tests an administrative request containing multiple typos.

email: La reunión del martes is now at 3 PM; please update the calendar invite.
expected_summary: The sender says Tuesday's meeting moved to 3 PM and requests a calendar update.
notes: Tests a mixed Spanish-English scheduling request outside the product categories.

email: Apparently changing my display name requires a grand ceremony; please set it to Maya.
expected_summary: The customer sarcastically asks to change the account display name to Maya.
notes: Tests an administrative profile change expressed sarcastically.

email: Please cancel tomorrow's meeting; our office is closed for the holiday.
expected_summary: The sender wants tomorrow's meeting cancelled because the office is closed.
notes: Tests routine scheduling administration unrelated to product sales or support.

email: I can access everything normally; I only need the account contact email changed.
expected_summary: The customer only wants the account contact email changed and reports no access problem.
notes: Tests other versus support by explicitly ruling out a technical issue.

email: I'm applying for the data analyst role and have attached my résumé.
expected_summary: The sender is applying for a data analyst position and attached a résumé.
notes: Tests a legitimate general business email outside all product-related categories.
